raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

On ROCm, every DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1 sparse-MLA decode `build()` packs its ragged indices into scratch tensors and then copies them into the FULL decode graph buffers, and the ROCm SWA builders cannot refresh those buffers after a draft step; this PR packs straight into the graph buffers and adds the in-place draft refresh, so the ROCm SWA builders set `supports_draft_decode_metadata_update = True`.

`build_ragged_indices_from_dense_out()` runs the count → scan → compact kernels from #58058 into caller-owned buffers, writing counts into `indptr[1:]` and scanning them in place; `build_ragged_indices_from_dense()` becomes an allocating wrapper, so the `-1` filtering has one implementation and prefill output is unchanged. `build_ragged_into_graph_buffers()` and `refresh_decode_swa_ragged()` sit beside it in `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` and are shared by the V4 C128A/SWA and V4.1 SWA builders; each ROCm SWA `update_draft_decode_metadata()` is `super()` plus one call. The gfx950 width narrowing is unchanged. The draft refresh comes from #52628 (Tres Popp, co-author), closed in favour of this PR.

When every draft attention group can update in place, the MRV2 draft speculators record the update in their FULL draft graph instead of rebuilding the draft metadata eagerly on every draft step; since #60692 that includes DSpark, whose draft layers are SWA-only on V4 and V4.1.

## Claims

- The packing runs 7 times per decode step on V4.1 and 3 on V4. Each call drops from 5 kernels, 3 allocations and 2 `hipMemcpyAsync` to 3 kernels, saving 14.2–14.6 µs (27 %) at every shape on MI355X.
- End to end on V4.1-Flash the effect is marginal: −1.5 % per verify step with DSpark and −0.4 % TPOT without spec at concurrency 1, within run-to-run spread at concurrency 4 and 64.
- All of it comes from the packing. The in-graph draft update removes main's eager draft rebuild (on 948 of 950 draft steps under DSpark) and its `Attention backend(s) DEEPSEEK_SPARSE_SWA cannot update draft decode metadata in place; falling back to rebuilding attention metadata eagerly.` log, but gives no measurable speedup: with the flag forced off, DSpark is within 0.5 % of the PR at every concurrency.
- GSM8K and DSpark acceptance agree with main as closely as a repeated main run does.

## Validation

Unit, MI355X (gfx950), main `5c4b94beec`, main's and the PR's `tests/` against each tree: the PR's tests pass on the PR; main's tests fail on the PR only where they import the removed `_copy_ragged_to_graph_buffers`; forcing the flag off fails only `test_rocm_swa_builder_enables_fused_draft_decode`; a no-op `refresh_decode_swa_ragged()` fails the four draft-update cases.

Micro, MI355X, main `5c4b94beec`, the production helpers at the e2e configs' V4.1 SWA shapes (1–384 rows × 128), 5 % `-1` sentinels, median of runs 2–4, same `indptr` and indices on both arms: main 53.5–53.9 µs per call, PR 39.0–39.4 µs, −14.2 to −14.6 µs (27 %) at every shape.

e2e, V4.1-Flash, TP=2, MI355X, main `5c4b94beec`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, DSpark as `{"method": "dspark"}`. `vllm bench serve`, random 1031 in / 509 out, 32 × concurrency prompts, one server on the host at a time, fresh server per run, median (range) of runs 2–4. "Flag off" is this PR with `supports_draft_decode_metadata_update = False`. With DSpark the metric is ms per verify step, mean TPOT × mean acceptance length: on random prompts acceptance moves between 1.64 and 1.94 from run to run, and raw TPOT and throughput follow it.

| concurrency | metric | main | flag off | PR | PR vs main |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | mean TPOT, ms | 6.76 (6.75–6.78) | – | 6.73 (6.65–6.74) | −0.4 % |
| 4 | median TPOT, ms | 8.34 (8.33–8.37) | – | 8.32 (8.31–8.33) | −0.2 % |
| 1, DSpark | ms / verify step | 9.64 (9.60–9.67) | 9.51 (9.46–9.55) | 9.49 (9.43–9.57) | −1.5 % |
| 4, DSpark | ms / verify step | 13.92 (13.75–13.92) | 13.83 (13.75–13.85) | 13.89 (13.84–13.92) | −0.2 % |
| 64, DSpark | ms / verify step | 50.78 (50.53–50.97) | 50.80 (50.47–50.82) | 50.79 (50.76–50.82) | 0.0 % |

GSM8K 5-shot strict-match, greedy, `seed=1234`, same setup:

| V4.1-Flash | main | main (repeat) | flag off | PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DSpark | 0.9303 | 0.9348 | 0.9265 | 0.9272 |
| DSpark mean acceptance length | 3.448 | 3.451 | 3.442 | 3.431 |
| no spec | 0.9219 | 0.9219 | – | 0.9227 |

Per sample, the PR matches main's verdict on 1265 of 1319 with DSpark (repeat 1259) and 1250 without (repeat 1257). V4 was last measured on main `72e7874fa6`, before #60692: at concurrency 61, TP=1 and MTP × 3, the arms' ranges overlapped and GSM8K matched main as closely as a repeat.

## Details

With `--monokernel` (off by default), V4.1 decode batches of up to 32 rows get their SWA metadata from `swa_decode_meta`, on gfx942 since #60731 and on gfx950 since #63885, which also writes into the graph buffers; this PR covers the default configuration, larger V4.1 batches, and V4. #57860 fuses indptr into a different V4.1 pack kernel and composes with this.

---

Found by [Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom); reviewed and measured by hand.

The draft-step body lives there as `refresh_decode_swa_ragged()`, so each ROCm SWA builder's `update_draft_decode_metadata()` is now `super()` plus one call. The draft-update unit test now runs on both the V4 and V4.1 builders, and its cases fail when `refresh_decode_swa_ragged()` is made a no-op.

When you wrote this, yes: V4.1 runs DSpark, and the flag only mattered for the MTP fused-AR draft path. #60692 (merged Oct 12) changed that. `DSparkSpeculator` subclasses `DFlashSpeculator`, which now checks `supports_draft_decode_metadata_update` on every draft attention group. If all of them support it, it records `update_draft_decode_metadata()` inside the FULL draft CUDA graph and skips the eager `_build_uniform_attn_metadata()` on replay.

The DSpark draft layers are SWA-only on both models: V4.1 treats layers past `compress_ratios` as ratio 0, and V4-Flash's entry at index 43 is 0. So their only builder is the ROCm SWA builder this PR enables, and on today's `main` the flag switches that path on for ROCm rather than being dead code.

That also raises the bar on validation. None of the Oct 1 numbers exercised this path, because they predate #60692. I'll rerun with DSpark before asking for another look.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v4.amd.rocm import (
+    DeepseekV4ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadataBuilder,
+    DeepseekV4ROCMAiterSparseSWAMetadata,
+    DeepseekV4ROCMAiterSparseSWAMetadataBuilder,
+)
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.rocm import (
+    DeepseekV41ROCMAiterSparseSWAMetadata,
+    DeepseekV41ROCMAiterSparseSWAMetadataBuilder,
+)
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.sparse_swa import (
+    DeepseekSparseSWAMetadataBuilder,
+)
+from vllm.v1.attention.ops import rocm_aiter_mla_sparse
+from vllm.v1.attention.ops.rocm_aiter_mla_sparse import (
+    build_ragged_indices_from_dense_out,
+)
+
+
+def _build_ragged_reference(
+    indices: torch.Tensor,
+    lengths: torch.Tensor,
+    num_rows: int = -1,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    rows = []
+    for row, length in zip(indices, lengths.tolist()):
+        row = row[: max(length, 0)]
+        keep = row >= 0
+        if num_rows >= 0:
+            keep &= row < num_rows
+        rows.append(row[keep])
+    ragged = torch.cat(rows) if rows else torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.int32)
+    indptr = torch.zeros(len(rows) + 1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    torch.cumsum(
+        torch.tensor([r.numel() for r in rows], dtype=torch.int32),
+        dim=0,
+        out=indptr[1:],
+    )
+    return ragged, indptr
+
+
+def _build_ragged_reference_out(
+    indices: torch.Tensor,
+    lengths: torch.Tensor,
+    out_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    out_indptr: torch.Tensor,
+) -> None:
+    ragged, indptr = _build_ragged_reference(indices, lengths)
+    out_indptr.copy_(indptr)
+    out_indices[: ragged.numel()].copy_(ragged)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("updated_indices", "updated_lens"),
+    [
+        (
+            [
+                [63, 64, 65, 66],
+                [127, 128, 129, 130],
+                [191, 192, 193, 194],
+                [255, 256, 257, 258],
+            ],

+    builder_cls: type,

+    updated_lens: list[int],
+):
+    builder = object.__new__(builder_cls)
+    dense_indices = torch.zeros((4, 1, 4), dtype=torch.int32)
+    dense_lens = torch.zeros(4, dtype=torch.int32)
+    ragged_indices = torch.full((16,), -1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    ragged_indptr = torch.full((5,), -1, dtype=torch.int32)

+        decode_swa_ragged_indptr=ragged_indptr,
+        num_decodes=4,
+        num_decode_tokens=4,
+    )
+    ragged_indices_ptr = ragged_indices.data_ptr()
+    ragged_indptr_ptr = ragged_indptr.data_ptr()
+
+    def update_dense(_builder, updated_metadata):
+        updated_metadata.decode_swa_indices.copy_(
+            torch.tensor(updated_indices, dtype=torch.int32).view(4, 1, 4)
+        )
+        updated_metadata.decode_swa_lens.copy_(
+            torch.tensor(updated_lens, dtype=torch.int32)
+        )
+
+    with (
+        patch.object(
+            DeepseekSparseSWAMetadataBuilder,
+            "update_draft_decode_metadata",
+            update_dense,
+        ),
+        patch.object(
+            rocm_aiter_mla_sparse,
+            "build_ragged_indices_from_dense_out",
+            _build_ragged_reference_out,
+        ),
+    ):
+        builder.update_draft_decode_metadata(metadata)
+
+    expected_indices, expected_indptr = _build_ragged_reference(
+        torch.tensor(updated_indices, dtype=torch.int32),
+        torch.tensor(updated_lens, dtype=torch.int32),

+    assert metadata.decode_swa_ragged_indptr is ragged_indptr

+    lengths: torch.Tensor,
+    num_rows: int = -1,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    flat = torch.empty(indices.numel(), dtype=torch.int32, device=indices.device)
+    indptr = torch.empty(indices.shape[0] + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device=indices.device)
+    build_ragged_indices_from_dense_out(indices, lengths, flat, indptr, num_rows)
     return flat, indptr
 
 
+class DecodeSWARaggedMetadata(Protocol):
+    num_decode_tokens: int
+    decode_swa_indices: torch.Tensor | None
+    decode_swa_lens: torch.Tensor | None
+    decode_swa_ragged_indices: torch.Tensor | None
+    decode_swa_ragged_indptr: torch.Tensor | None
+
+
+def build_ragged_into_graph_buffers(
+    dense_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    dense_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    ragged_indices_buffer: torch.Tensor,
+    ragged_indptr_buffer: torch.Tensor,
+    num_rows: int,
+    max_entries_per_row: int,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Pack dynamic ragged metadata into persistent CUDA graph buffers.
+
+    FULL decode graphs capture kernel argument addresses. Keep the returned
+    tensors backed by stable storage, while indptr continues to bound reads.
+    """
+    dense = dense_indices.reshape(dense_indices.shape[0], -1)
+    build_ragged_indices_from_dense_out(
+        dense, dense_lens, ragged_indices_buffer, ragged_indptr_buffer
+    )
+    indptr_out = ragged_indptr_buffer[: num_rows + 1]
+    if _ON_GFX950:
+        # Preserve the graph-stable base pointer while exposing source capacity
+        # to the sync-free split selector; indptr still carries the true NNZ.
+        return ragged_indices_buffer[: max(dense.numel(), 1)], indptr_out
+    return ragged_indices_buffer[: max(num_rows * max_entries_per_row, 1)], indptr_out
+
+
+def refresh_decode_swa_ragged(metadata: DecodeSWARaggedMetadata) -> None:
+    """Repack the decode SWA ragged indices in place after a draft step."""
+    if metadata.num_decode_tokens == 0:
+        return
+    assert metadata.decode_swa_indices is not None
+    assert metadata.decode_swa_lens is not None
+    assert metadata.decode_swa_ragged_indices is not None
+    assert metadata.decode_swa_ragged_indptr is not None
+    build_ragged_indices_from_dense_out(
+        metadata.decode_swa_indices.reshape(metadata.num_decode_tokens, -1),
+        metadata.decode_swa_lens,
+        metadata.decode_swa_ragged_indices,
+        metadata.decode_swa_ragged_indptr,
+    )
+
+
 def _as_int32_contiguous_1d(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
     if x.dtype == torch.int32 and x.ndim == 1 and x.is_contiguous():
         return x

The draft-step body lives there as `refresh_decode_swa_ragged()`, so each ROCm SWA builder's `update_draft_decode_metadata()` is now `super()` plus one call. The draft-update unit test now runs on both the V4 and V4.1 builders, and its cases fail when `refresh_decode_swa_ragged()` is made a no-op.

When you wrote this, yes: V4.1 runs DSpark, and the flag only mattered for the MTP fused-AR draft path. #60692 (merged Oct 12) changed that. `DSparkSpeculator` subclasses `DFlashSpeculator`, which now checks `supports_draft_decode_metadata_update` on every draft attention group. If all of them support it, it records `update_draft_decode_metadata()` inside the FULL draft CUDA graph and skips the eager `_build_uniform_attn_metadata()` on replay.

The DSpark draft layers are SWA-only on both models: V4.1 treats layers past `compress_ratios` as ratio 0, and V4-Flash's entry at index 43 is 0. So their only builder is the ROCm SWA builder this PR enables, and on today's `main` the flag switches that path on for ROCm rather than being dead code.

That also raises the bar on validation. None of the Oct 1 numbers exercised this path, because they predate #60692. I'll rerun with DSpark before asking for another look.
